_why.why_chosen: Two defects in DIFFERENT field types - a port and a number - so it exercises both normalisation paths in one email, where a two-name defect would only exercise one. It also carries the locode decoy: the port of discharge changes from FREMANTLE, AUSTRALIA to BUSAN, SOUTH KOREA while the code (AUFRE) stays identical on both sides. A rule that compares the code finds nothing here.
_why.covers: MISMATCH across two field types, and the UN/LOCODE decoy on ports
_why.assert_this: defect_fields is exactly {port_of_discharge, container_count}. The port must be flagged even though the locode matches, and the container count must compare 6 against 5, not the full "6 x 20'GP" string. End-to-end credit needs the exact set, so a superset scores zero.
_why.caveat: Our reading of the documents, not an organiser label.
